A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CT-MLE research, with matching authors, core algorithms, and retained figures. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 Appendix C reports original experiments on Pendulum, Cart Pole, and Acrobot, including measurement-gap selection, episodes to success, and reward-error curves.

after.justification: v2 Appendix C retains those empirical results and adds comparisons against ENODE and SAC-TaCoS and a neural-network-width ablation.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 remain essentially unchanged, but v2 introduces Lagrangian CT-MLE in Algorithm 3. Its practical model objective adds a policy-value term to v1's sliced score-matching loss and replaces hard likelihood constraints with penalties. This substantively changes the practical learning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate noisy Pendulum, Cart Pole, and Acrobot. The new comparisons use sigma = 2.0, already included in v1's noise sweep, and the width study reuses Pendulum. v2 explicitly describes fully actuated Acrobot, but v1 does not specify actuation sufficiently to establish a changed variant.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates CT-MLE without reported competitor results. v2 Appendix C.2 and Figure 2 add actual comparisons against ENODE and SAC-TaCoS across all three control environments; their earlier citations were not empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds a comparative reward-curve protocol at sigma = 2.0 with 5, 15, and 15 training episodes for Pendulum, CartPole, and Acrobot, respectively. It specifies comparator measurement strategies, annealed Lagrange multipliers, and a controlled width sweep. The original noise/gap success protocol remains; the new budgets do not establish that its runs were shortened.

E4.justification: v2 adds a Pendulum sensitivity study varying dynamics-network width through 150, 175, 200, 225, and 250 hidden units while holding other components fixed. The existing stochasticity/measurement-gap and convergence analyses are retained, although reorganized under Appendix C.3.

E5.justification: The retained analyses preserve their seed counts and mean plus/minus one standard error reporting: 10 Pendulum seeds and 5 Cart Pole/Acrobot seeds. The new comparisons continue standard-error reporting, and the five-seed width study extends the existing multiseed practice without introducing a new uncertainty procedure or revising existing run counts.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds comparative reward curves reporting higher late-training rewards for CT-MLE and faster initial learning for SAC-TaCoS. Figure 4 adds similar final returns across five network widths. v1 Figures 2–3 are retained unchanged as v2 Figures 3 and 5; the added curves are new results under newly specified protocols.

T1.justification: v2 removes the finite-class restriction from Assumption 5.1, introduces bracketing numbers in Definition 5.6, and replaces cardinality-based confidence calibration with bracketing-based calibration in Theorem 5.11. Proposition 5.10, Appendix A.2, and new confidence-set lemmas substantially expand the formal treatment beyond v1's brief remark about infinite classes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: marginal-density MLE, variance- and measurement-dependent regret, and randomized observations preserving the order of measurement complexity. The added theory and experiments support these retained contributions without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing ENODE's weak performance to stochastic environments and the width-ablation findings to architectural robustness. It removes v1's statement that benchmark empirical validation is still needed. Limitations concerning computational guarantees, online variance adaptation, known rewards, and stationary policies remain.

D1.justification: v1 already documents score matching, RK45, AdamW, hardware, and core hyperparameters. v2 substantially expands this with planning-gradient calculations, combined model updates, multiplier annealing, a 10:1 loss-scaling target, and ensemble/policy/critic architectures in Table 2. Existing hardware and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Geer (2000) for bracketing numbers and Zhong and Leonard (2020) for the Acrobot setup, and expands discussion of the evaluated baselines. The main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; citation-style and bibliographic updates are presentational.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introduction and experimental prose, adds a main-text proof sketch and ethics/reproducibility/LLM statements, and reorganizes Appendix C into implementation, main results, ablations, and additional details. Most of the main narrative and existing proof exposition remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, title/author arrangement, running headers, and heading typography. It adds the Algorithm 3 display, comparator and width-ablation plots, and an architecture table. Existing experimental figures are relocated and renumbered, with the convergence plot placed beside the new ablation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's illustrative experiments, v2 provides direct baseline evidence, a width sensitivity check, and a clearer practical optimization specification, improving empirical assessability and implementation transparency. However, guarantees still concern Algorithm 1 rather than practical Algorithm 3. The new Proposition 5.10 proof also uses an unjustified ordering-after-squaring step in Equation A.6 for its allowed signed matrices, limiting the quality gain from the theoretical extension.
